content.comment_body: Hello, I need to read 16 analog inputs from multiple sensors and display the values on a panel. Since the maximum analog inputs for a [product_name] is 8, is it possible to connect three [product_name] devices together in a network to achieve 24 analog inputs? Thanks for your help.

No, that's not feasible. A [product_name] with [article_no] can handle up to 8 analog inputs; adding more is not supported. If you need additional analog inputs, for example 8 more, you'll need a separate [product_name] device.

There are multiple technical solutions to this issue. Exploring options outside of [company_name] products can yield useful alternatives. For example, searching for 'modbus tcp analog input' online brings up several possibilities. Many panel brands are able to directly read data from Modbus TCP devices.
Thank you for your response. I'm planning to use three [product_name] devices to increase the number of analog inputs. I just need to verify that my panel can handle up to five IP addresses.
That's interesting, I'll look into those other products. Thanks a lot.

analysis.insight_summary: Users point out a hardware limit of 8 analog inputs per [product_name] device. Discussions focus on ways to scale beyond this, such as linking multiple devices or considering alternatives outside the [company_name] lineup. There's clear interest in solutions that allow for system expansion and compatibility with panel devices.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope for an easy method to increase analog inputs beyond the hardware limitation, and want to integrate this expanded setup with their panel without additional complexity.
